children: DnB Bank said it expects to improve profitability over the next three years as it cuts costs and develops its use of artificial intelligence.

Ahead of its capital markets day Tuesday, the Norwegian lender said it is targeting a return on equity above 15% for 2029, with a cost-income ratio below 38%, a common equity Tier 1 capital ratio above 16.3% and a payout ratio higher than 50%.
The bank aims to deliver on the targets by the end of 2028.

DnB has existing financial targets for a return on equity of over 14% and a cost-income ratio below 40%, which it said would be maintained for 2027 and 2028. It hopes to make "gradual progress" toward the new targets throughout the 2027 to 2029 period.
Targets for CET1 capital ratio--a measure of financial strength--and dividend policy will remain unchanged throughout the period.
DnB also targets annual lending growth between 3% and 4% over time, with annual growth in net commission and fee income over 9% through the cycle.

"DnB has a strong position, and over time we have proven that we deliver on our financial targets. Now we will continue to build on our leading positions in Norway, while also exploring the opportunities provided by a strengthened Nordic platform," Chief Executive Officer Kjerstin Braathen said.
